clue.text: Italian's so long in Chicago, oddly

indicators.note: taking only the odd-numbered letters of the city's name, first, third, fifth and seventh

parts.note: the city name supplies the letters to be thinned out

explanation.surface: An Italian says goodbye somewhere in the Windy City.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian farewell word, also borrowed into English, is a casual way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Be irritating about length — he tends to exaggerate it

indicators.note: the irritation word goes round the letter for length, surrounding it

parts.note: to anger someone is to annoy or irritate them

explanation.surface: Someone who annoys people by boasting about the length of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'it' of the definition is the length mentioned in the wordplay: the fish that got away always grows in the telling.
explanation.definitionFit: A fisherman is famous for inflating the size of his catch when telling the story afterwards.

clue.text: As which, best is the same as worst

definitions.text: As which, best is the same as worst

parts.note: asks what part of speech the two words are being treated as

parts.words: best is the same as worst
parts.note: looks paradoxical, but used as action words both mean to defeat someone

explanation.walkthrough: To best someone and to worst someone both mean to beat them, so the opposites only agree when used as doing words.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words can function as transitive grammatical action words meaning defeat or get the better of.

clue.text: Indication you need a sling after fracture

indicators.note: the letters are broken and reset in a new order, as a bone would be after a fracture

parts.note: the two words are the raw letters to be broken and reset

explanation.surface: A sign that your broken arm needs to go in a sling.
explanation.walkthrough: The medical picture makes 'fracture' look like an injury, but it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal is a sign or gesture that conveys information, which is an indication.

clue.text: Intimidated, old woman got married

parts.note: Vera is a woman's name, standing for any woman
to wed is to marry

explanation.surface: An elderly woman felt daunted when she tied the knot.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overawed means being subdued or made timid by awe or fear, so it amounts to being intimidated.

clue.text: Father was furious after daughter is denigrated

indicators.note: the father's fury is placed after the daughter piece

parts.note: taken as written
pa is a familiar word for father
raged means was furious

explanation.surface: Dad lost his temper once his daughter was belittled.
explanation.definitionFit: To disparage someone is to speak of them slightingly, so it is a synonym of belittle or run down.

clue.text: Highest level of salt in tree

indicators.note: the salt formula sits inside the tree name

parts.note: the pine is a conifer
NaCl is the chemical formula for common salt, sodium chloride

explanation.surface: Asks about the peak concentration of salt found in a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle is a mountain peak, and figuratively the summit or culmination of something.

clue.text: Part of our capital, in addition, invested in tea

indicators.note: to be invested in is to be clothed in, so one word goes inside the tea word

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
else means besides or in addition

explanation.surface: Reads like a financial note about money put into a tea business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our capital' is London from a British paper's viewpoint; Chelsea is a district of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea is a well-known district of west London, the British capital city, so it is a part of that city.

clue.text: Unsuccessfully leading army maybe around island

indicators.note: the leading-army phrase goes around the island letter

parts.note: the van is the front of an army, so to lead is to be in the van

explanation.surface: A general fails to lead his troops around an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in vain means doing it to no avail, without any success.

clue.text: Dog in cargo vessel that's docked

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the ship's name loses its last letter

parts.note: a collier is a ship that carries coal

explanation.surface: A dog is aboard a freighter that has come into port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Docked' suggests a ship tied up in harbour, but here it means cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: The collie is a Scottish herding breed of canine, used as a sheepdog.

clue.text: Cleaned out bunk — part needs to be remade

indicators.note: remaking the bed means putting its letters together again differently

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bunk bed is stripped and part of it has to be rebuilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cleaned out is an informal idiom for having lost all one's money, i.e. being insolvent.

clue.text: Performer who survives dangerous form of consumption?

definitions.text: Performer who survives dangerous form of consumption?

parts.note: a circus or street entertainer who lives through each act
consumption suggests the disease tuberculosis, but here it is literal eating of a blade

explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumption' was an old name for tuberculosis, a dangerous illness; here it means putting something down the throat, namely a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: This entertainer passes a long blade down the throat, a perilous act of apparent eating.

clue.text: Timepiece that, on the other hand, can be digitally adjusted

definitions.text: Timepiece that, on the other hand, can be digitally adjusted

parts.words: Timepiece that, on the other hand
parts.note: sounds like 'however', but it is literal: worn on the hand you do not write with
suggests a digital display, but means set with the fingers

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the other hand' looks like a turn of phrase and 'digitally' like electronics; both are literal, about the arm and fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: This timekeeper is strapped to the arm, usually the non-dominant one, and set by turning the crown with fingers.

clue.text: A medic taken around hospital for particular purpose

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the medic is put around the hospital letter, enclosing it

parts.note: doc is short for doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor is shown around a hospital for a specific reason.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase describes something arranged for one specific need only, not as a general rule.

clue.text: Family doctor, primarily caring

parts.note: kin are one's relatives

indicators.note: only the leading letter of the following word is used

parts.note: only the opening letter of this word is taken

explanation.surface: A family doctor whose first concern is looking after patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family doctor' reads as one GP but splits into relatives and a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Kind and caring are adjective synonyms describing a considerate, warm-hearted nature.

clue.text: Like theatre surgeon, perhaps, caught pocketing fine instrument

indicators.note: the doctor and catch letters hold the instrument in their pocket, surrounding it

parts.note: a surgeon is an example of a doctor, abbreviated
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
an Amati is a violin made by the famous Amati family of Cremona

explanation.surface: A surgeon in an operating theatre is caught stealing a precious violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' and 'surgeon' paint an operating theatre, but the definition means stage drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Dramatic means relating to drama, the art of the stage, so it is like the theatre.

clue.text: A cold that man had caused discomfort

parts.note: taken as written
he'd is the contraction of he had

explanation.surface: A man's cold made him feel ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that ached gave a dull continuous pain, so it caused bodily discomfort.

clue.text: Diamonds I spread out for show

parts.note: taken as written
to splay is to spread out, as fingers or legs

explanation.surface: Jewels laid out to be shown off.
explanation.definitionFit: A display is an exhibition or public presentation, so as a noun it is a synonym of show.

clue.text: Nasty cracks in accommodation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: snide remarks or jibes
second meaning: British slang for rented lodgings

explanation.surface: Unpleasant cracks appearing in rented rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: Digs is everyday British slang for lodgings, typically a rented room.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a plural of jibe-like remarks and informal British slang for lodgings.

clue.text: Middle-of-the-road positions on which it's safe to take a stand?

definitions.text: Middle-of-the-road positions on which it's safe to take a stand?

parts.note: sounds like moderate political views, but means places literally in mid-carriageway

parts.words: on which it's safe to take a stand
parts.note: taking a stand suggests holding firm opinions; here it is literally standing safe from cars

explanation.walkthrough: The political sense of 'middle-of-the-road' and 'take a stand' is the decoy; read literally they describe raised refuges in a street.
explanation.definitionFit: These are raised kerbed areas in the centre of a street where pedestrians can wait out of the vehicles' path.

clue.text: Hesitate as female tailor

parts.note: to tailor or alter clothes is to adjust them

explanation.surface: Wavering just like a female dressmaker does.
explanation.definitionFit: To falter is to waver or lose resolve, a close synonym of hesitate.

clue.text: In audience for Shakespeare, namely As You Like It?

parts.note: being at an event means being in its audience
Will is the Bard's first name

explanation.surface: Watching a Shakespeare play, namely As You Like It.
explanation.walkthrough: The play title is the definition, read as an ordinary phrase rather than a comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at will means doing it whenever or however one pleases, just as one likes.

clue.text: Men and boys outside prison put back in shackles

indicators.note: the male word sits outside the reversed prison, enclosing it

parts.note: males covers men and boys together

indicators.note: the prison word is put back to front

parts.note: can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Male prisoners are sent back to jail and clapped in irons.
explanation.definitionFit: Manacles are metal restraints for the wrists, a synonym of shackles or handcuffs.

clue.text: Second nature for so-called lawyer

parts.note: ilk means type or kind, the nature of something

explanation.surface: Suggests a lawyer's second nature, as if habits came with the job.
explanation.walkthrough: A silk is a King's (or Queen's) Counsel, a senior British barrister, named after the silk gown worn.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior barristers are nicknamed after their silk gowns, so the word is a so-called name for such an advocate.

clue.text: Line outstanding, calling from Jersey or Guernsey

parts.note: a debt still owing is outstanding

explanation.surface: Reads like a telephone line still owing for calls from the Channel Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey and Guernsey look like the islands, but they are also breeds of dairy cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowing is the mooing sound cattle make, and Jersey and Guernsey are cow breeds.

clue.text: Something found in Chinese soup — or in minestrone

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the Italian soup's name

parts.note: the soup's name conceals the answer in its middle letters

explanation.surface: Compares ingredients of Chinese soup with those of minestrone.
explanation.walkthrough: Bird's nest soup is a Chinese delicacy made from swiftlet saliva nests.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible birds' homes made by swiftlets are the key ingredient of a famous Chinese delicacy soup.

clue.text: Energetic kind of voice

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the grammatical voice in which the subject performs the action

explanation.walkthrough: 'Voice' suggests singing, but this is grammar: active versus passive.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for lively people and the grammatical voice contrasting with passive.

clue.text: Alternative to ally is supporter of ruler

indicators.note: an alternative arrangement of the letters is called for

parts.note: these three words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Choosing to side with a monarch rather than rebels.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyalist is one who stays faithful to the established sovereign or government, especially in revolt.
